<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, the IR spectrum is the most direct and inexpensive method because carbonyl groups give a characteristic strong absorption near 1700 cm⁻¹. By examining the IR peaks we can count how many distinct carbonyl stretches are present, which corresponds to the number of carbonyl groups in the molecule.</thought>
